source.title: Belief or Circuitry? Causal Evidence for In-Context Graph Learning
source.authors: Katharine Kowalyshyn; T. Duggan; D. Little; M. C. Hughes

page_placements.theme: ICL that copying can't explain runs through FFNs, other subspaces or non-induction heads

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study investigates graph-structure learning and discusses induction circuits as a competing or complementary account, but it does not measure induction heads, token-copying behaviour, or the loss-by-token-index effect named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on graph-neighbor prediction, graph representations, and interventions on graph-family signals. These results are recorded as findings about graph ICL, but they do not directly measure the induction-head behaviours or training dynamics specified by the claim versions. The paper also cites prior findings about induction circuits and phase transitions; those cited results are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study tests graph-random-walk next-node prediction in Llama-3.1-8B. It uses behavioural sigmoid fits, PCA of the residual stream, residual patching and steering. It argues that induction circuits alone cannot explain the results. However, it never identifies, ablates or measures induction heads, prefix-matching/copying scores, previous-token composition, training dynamics, or loss by token index. Its anti-induction arguments are inferences from predicted signatures (λ̂>0, topology asymmetry, orthogonal subspaces, held-out-edge patching), not measurements of how much the heads contribute. Head-level ablations are named as future work. It therefore does not test any version; its findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Llama-3.1-8B is neither a pure structure learner nor a pure induction-cache machine. They favour a dual mechanism in which induction-like caches and latent-structure representations operate together. They note that the delayed held-out effects suggest local transition evidence still matters.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines graph-family inference, residual-stream geometry, activation patching, and steering in a pretrained Llama model; it does not reproduce the original induction-head identification or training-phase measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported graph-family steering effect varies with steering strength α and layer; patching recovery also varies across the selected layers. The paper reports different vocabulary conditions for behavioral fitting and a closed-vocabulary mixture condition for the PCA result.

fits_no_version.finding: Belief-dynamics fits give λ̂>0 and b̂grid<b̂ring in both vocabulary conditions. The grid inflection point shifts later as the ring mixture rises, and the ring converges faster at ρ=1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On graph random-walk ICL, Llama-3.1-8B shows topology-sensitive, complexity-weighted evidence accumulation. The authors argue uniform transition-copying would not produce this.

fits_no_version.finding: At ρ=0.5, layer-26 class-mean PCA is described as encoding both graph topologies in orthogonal subspaces. The Dirichlet energy reported rose from 0.785 to 0.828.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream geometry carries graph-topology information for multiple in-context graphs simultaneously (qualitative evidence).

fits_no_version.finding: Late-layer final-position patching recovers 0.987 of the clean graph-family contrast. The held-out-edge contrast turns positive by layer 26 (0.492) and reaches 2.0 at layer 30. Steering at α=5 recovers 0.449, while random and shuffled-label controls stay near 0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A manipulable graph-family representation in late residual layers causally drives graph-neighbor predictions, including for edges unseen in the corrupt context.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 9th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The causal experiments and representational analyses use Llama-3.1-8B; the authors say head-level ablations and scaling to larger Llama models remain future work. The overlap behavioral fit's b0 estimate saturated its lower search bound, and the reported Dirichlet-energy increase is in tension with the stated interpretation that lower energy indicates stronger adjacency alignment. The PCA evidence is principally qualitative.

untested.parts: No previous-token heads, induction heads, or [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying are identified; the model is not small or attention-only.
No training dynamics; only a pretrained checkpoint is used. The context-length 'phase transition' is not a training-time phase change.
Induction heads' share of in-context learning, and per-token loss decrease, are not measured. Head-level ablations are deferred to future work.
Only one model; induction behaviour is not measured.
Training data and setup are not varied. Mixture ratio and vocabulary are varied only in context, at inference.
No few-shot task learning, and no comparison of induction heads with other heads.
Formation of induction heads over training is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: Claims about induction heads (e.g., Arditi 2026 identifying induction heads in Llama-3.1-8B) are cited, not this study's results. Model selection by AIC/BIC is reported without numbers. The b0 lower-bound saturation in the overlap fit may bias λ̂ toward zero in that condition.

versions.untested_parts: No induction heads are identified or tested for previous-token-head composition or [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying.
No induction-head formation over training, training-loss bump, or timing comparison with an in-context-learning gain is measured.

The study does not measure induction heads' contribution to most in-context learning, nor loss falling with token index. Its graph-neighbor prediction and graph-family interventions do not quantify the share of ICL carried by induction heads.
The study uses Llama-3.1-8B and does not test induction behaviour across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
It varies graph mixture and vocabulary conditions, but does not test whether induction-head formation or ICL persistence depends on training data or training setup.
It does not test few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other mechanisms on that behaviour.
It does not resolve induction-head formation into sub-steps or measure multiple overlapping formation transitions.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit the complexity-weighted belief-dynamics model to graph-neighbor accuracy curves.
rows.measure: Fitted complexity penalty λ̂ and graph prior terms
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: λ̂ > 0 and b̂grid < b̂ring in both vocabulary conditions
rows.note: The paper interprets the fitted inequality as a complexity-sensitive structural bias; it does not report the fitted parameter values here.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compare grid and ring inflection points as the ring mixture increases.
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: The grid's N* shifts monotonically later as ring evidence increases
rows.note: No numeric inflection points are given in the main text.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compare fitted graph-specific dynamics with a mixture-bias ablation.
rows.measure: Relative convergence speed of ring and grid fits
rows.baseline: grid
rows.value: The ring converges faster than the grid
rows.note: The authors relate the faster ring convergence to its lower MDL complexity; no numeric convergence rates are stated.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measure degree-normalized Dirichlet energy of layer-26 residual-stream class-mean activations.
rows.baseline: 0.785 at short context
rows.note: The paper says lower Enorm indicates adjacent nodes are closer, but reports an increase from 0.785 to 0.828; it also describes the graph topology as recoverable at T = 1400.
rows.check: The baseline value 0.785 has no stated context length. The increase to 0.828 contradicts the paper's own statement that lower energy means more structure, so the state is correctly undeterminable.

rows.baseline: not stated

rows.note: The paper states this result in the text; it does not provide a numeric subspace-separation measure.

relation.reason: Induction circuits are discussed as an explanatory hypothesis; head-level ablations are proposed as future work.

tranche.reason: The study measures graph prediction and residual-stream interventions without identifying or testing induction heads. Its argument against a purely local copying account does not establish whether induction heads carry most token-index loss improvement or few-shot learning.

source_check.notes: The numerical results and authors' dual-mechanism conclusion are accurately represented. Held-out edges are absent from the corrupt context; these interventions do not establish induction heads' causal contribution.
